title: CARE-PO: Controllable Tool-Call Efficiency for LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.12125v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: External tool calls are a major running cost of an LLM agent, while its training objectives align almost exclusively with task completion. In a step-level diagnosis of Qwen3.5 trajectories at two model sizes on GAIA, a long-horizon tool-use benchmark, we find that most contain removable calls, at a similar rate at both sizes. Some methods add an efficiency reward to the objective to reduce the call count, but introduce problems of their own: the anchor they price calls against is computed from the policy's own rollouts (e.g., the group's shortest correct rollout) and so moves with the policy; training can drift toward a collapsed policy that issues no tool call at all, a degeneracy seen in published reports and in our 27B baseline; and a training run delivers a single operating point, so the user cannot trade efficiency against capability. We present CARE-PO (Controllable Anchored Relative Efficiency Policy Optimization) to mit

translated_title: CARE-PO：面向LLM智能体的可控工具调用效率
translated_abstract: 外部工具调用是LLM智能体运行成本的主要组成部分，然而其训练目标却几乎只与任务完成度对齐。我们在GAIA（一个长程工具使用基准）上对两种模型规模的Qwen3.5轨迹进行了步骤级诊断，发现大多数轨迹都包含可移除的调用，且两种规模下的比率相近。一些方法通过在目标函数中加入效率奖励来减少调用次数，但自身也引入了新问题：它们为调用定价所依据的锚点是从策略自身的rollout中计算得出的（例如该组中最短的正确rollout），因此会随策略移动；训练可能漂移向一个完全不再发出任何工具调用的坍缩策略——这种退化现象在已发表的报告中以及我们的27B基线模型中均有出现；此外，一次训练运行只能提供一个单一的工作点，用户无法在效率与能力之间进行权衡取舍。我们提出CARE-PO（Controllable Anchored Relative Efficiency Policy Optimization，可控锚定相对效率策略优化）来缓解上述问题（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 提出CARE-PO方法，通过可控的锚定相对效率策略优化，解决现有工具调用效率奖励训练中锚点随策略漂移、策略坍缩为不调用工具、以及单一工作点无法在效率与能力间权衡的三大问题。
en_tdlr: CARE-PO introduces controllable anchored relative efficiency policy optimization to overcome moving anchors, policy collapse, and single-operating-point limitations in efficiency-rewarded training of LLM agents' tool calls.
